facts.text: In 1879, Lawrence Gilman moved the Kent House to a new site, turning it into the Gardnerville Hotel and giving the town its name.
Danish settlers were among the first Europeans to shape Gardnerville’s early development, bringing agricultural techniques that still influence the valley today.
Spanish and French Basques arrived in 1898, becoming prominent sheepherders and later opening inns and restaurants that still echo in Gardnerville’s culinary scene.
The historic Jacobs Family Berry Farm, located in Gardnerville, is known for producing some of the best raspberries, blackberries, and black raspberries in the region.
Modern Gardnerville balances its heritage by serving as the business hub of Carson Valley while still celebrating its Basque roots and historic inns.
Gardnerville emerged in 1879 amid a local economic downturn and marital discord, yet its founders envisioned a thriving future on a dry sagebrush plain.
